correctness.rationale: A fully specified order-preserving projection partitions the augmented face poset. Hub fibers admit free subdivision-vertex toggles; no-hub fibers reduce to disjoint forbidden pairs and free isolated subdivision vertices. All but the all-selected u-pattern and (only for even n) the two cyclically alternating patterns admit complete acyclic fiber matchings. The remaining faces all have exactly n vertices; the patchwork theorem guarantees global acyclicity and dropping the empty-face pair yields one zero-cell plus 1 or 3 (n-1)-cells. Since n>=3, all attachments are constant and give the asserted integral wedges. Standalone exact Hasse acyclicity and chain computations at n<=9 corroborate without being mistaken for infinite proof.

The closest crown-graph dissociation, wheel-Mycielskian ordinary-independence, and fan matching-complex claims concern different complexes or graph families, and their statements do not imply the one-versus-three (n-1)-sphere type. value.rationale: Gear graphs form a canonical unbounded family combining a universal hub with a uniformly subdivided cyclic rim, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice. Relative to the natural 2026 higher-independence literature on trees and existing path/cycle families, the first higher-independence complex of gear graphs supplies a motivated missing homotopy classification. One sphere for odd n versus three for even n, in degree n-1, gives structural information not determined by graph nomenclature or Euler-characteristic data. The proof explains the parity via the two alternating hub-free patterns, a potentially reusable mechanism.
